qualification: MIDI complete packet endpoint2200ms and XM480ms include their release windows. Previously exact/beyond endpoints return the last release packet and XM i64MAX seek overflows its millisecond-to-microsecond multiplication. Six precise failures reproduce on existing authored synthetic controls.

MIDI clamps to packet_count rather than packet_count-1 with checked usize conversion. XM checks complete release endpoint before converting time and uses saturating multiplication for the remaining search. At/beyond complete end returns the exhausted cursor; score-end and release-window seeks remain available.

In-range targets0,1,lastmillisecond preserve encoded packet bytes and landing. Native full synthesis is the consistency baseline for actual worker play/rewind and empty complete-EOF seek; this is not a reference-quality synthesizer claim.

Existing authored MIDI/XM references are hashed and read in place. A short authored VP9/PCM companion decodes natively; these regressions concern timeline audio readers, not embedding MIDI/XM in a video container. Five SMF/six XM units, related integrations, fixture reproducibility and player build pass.

Score duration metadata is unchanged in this item and can differ from the complete release timeline. Release windows intentionally remain present. No32bit runtime, physical DAC, performance or codec-accuracy claim.
compatibility: Seek beyond the whole rendered/release timeline now reaches EOF rather than revisiting the release packet. In-range and score-end release behavior remain; no public signatures change.
counting: One bounded timeline seek cursor issue including XM overflow at an extreme beyond-end target; no extra IDs for variants or units.
